purpose: Couple distinct rank-3 clauses before the hard solve. Saturate resolution while retaining only clauses of width at most three, harvest every derived unit/binary consequence into the bijunctive layer, then rerun the implication-primitive reduction. This is an exact polynomial preprocessing theorem, not a complete resolution solver.
input: A terminal kernel F=H AND F3 on n terminal variables, where H is 2-CNF and every clause of F3 has width three.

width3_closure.universe: All non-tautological clauses of width at most three over n variables. Their number is sum_{i=0}^3 2^i * binom(n,i)=O(n^3).
width3_closure.rule: Whenever C union {x} and D union {NOT x} are present, form the resolvent C union D. Discard tautologies and resolvents of width greater than three; otherwise insert the resolvent if new.
width3_closure.termination: At most O(n^3) distinct clauses can ever be inserted, so naive repeated pair saturation is polynomial (for example O(n^9) with no optimization).
width3_closure.certificate: Store one parent pair and pivot for each newly inserted clause. If the empty clause appears, the resulting resolution DAG is a polynomial-size exact UNSAT certificate.

binary_extraction.definition: Let B be the set of all unit and binary clauses in the saturated width-3 closure.
binary_extraction.action: Replace the current bijunctive layer H by H union B, then apply the v3.8 implication-primitive normal-form rules to the original genuine 3-clauses.
binary_extraction.soundness: Every member of B is a resolution consequence of F, so adding B preserves the model set exactly. The v3.8 transformations are equivalences relative to the strengthened H.

theorem.name: WIDTH3_RESOLUTION_BINARY_CONSEQUENCE_KERNEL
theorem.statement: The procedure runs in deterministic polynomial time, preserves SAT/UNSAT and polynomial witness reconstruction, detects every refutation admitting a resolution proof of width at most three, and otherwise returns an equivalent implication-primitive terminal kernel enriched by every unit/binary consequence derivable through width-at-most-three resolution.
theorem.cross_clause_example: From (a OR b OR c) and (a OR b OR NOT c), width-3 resolution derives (a OR b). This binary consequence is invisible to v3.8 when H is initially empty, but after extraction it makes both ternary clauses redundant.
proof: Resolution is sound, hence every inserted clause is entailed by the input.
The clause universe has polynomial cardinality for fixed width three, proving termination and polynomial construction time.
If the empty clause is derived, soundness gives UNSAT and the stored parent DAG verifies the refutation in polynomial time.
If no empty clause is derived, adjoining all derived unit/binary clauses does not remove any model because they are logical consequences.
Applying v3.8 after this augmentation preserves equivalence and reconstruction by its theorem.
At saturation, every unit/binary clause possessing a width-at-most-three resolution derivation is present by closure under the only inference rule of resolution.

scientific_ceiling_and_barrier.not_complete: Fixed width is not a universal refutation bound. Ben-Sasson--Wigderson width lower bounds and later 3-CNF width-restricted lower bounds exhibit unsatisfiable bounded-width CNFs whose resolution refutations require width growing with n; Tseitin formulas on constant-degree expanders have linear resolution width.
scientific_ceiling_and_barrier.consequence: Failure to derive the empty clause at width three is SILENCE, not evidence of SAT. No P=NP claim follows from this closure.

next_target.name: E8_WIDTH3_CLOSED_PRIMITIVE_HYPERIMPLICATION_CORE_V4_0
next_target.directive: Attack only kernels surviving terminal projection, implication-primitive reduction, and complete width-3 resolution saturation. Every remaining 3-clause is genuinely ternary even after all width-3 cross-clause reasoning. Seek a global contraction/minimax invariant outside fixed-width resolution that either reduces the number of surviving ternary atoms or returns an exact polynomial UNSAT certificate.

sources: E. Ben-Sasson and A. Wigderson, Short Proofs are Narrow - Resolution made Simple, ECCC TR99-022 / JACM 2001.
E. Ben-Sasson and J. Johannsen, Lower bounds for width-restricted clause learning on small width formulas, ECCC TR10-085 (2010).
